question: What past performance information is required?
answer: Offerors must provide past performance information based on whether CPARS records exist:  - **CPARS exists:** If the Government has interim or final CPARS ratings for a claimed project, the offeror must include a copy of the rating report with its proposal. The Government may verify it in the CPARS database. [2][4] - **No CPARS, or non-federal project:** The offeror must submit an Attachment J.P-6 (A3 Past Performance Rating Template). No other format or additional documentation will be considered. [2][5] - **Template requirements:** The offeror must send the J.P-6 directly to each reference. It must be completed and signed by a Cognizant Contracting Officer or Government official, or by a Corporate Officer/Official for non-federal projects. It must include the rater's POC information, with a direct telephone number and email address. Raters must send completed forms directly back to the offeror, and all templates must be submitted with the proposal. [2][5][6] - **Unable to obtain a record:** For any Primary NAICS Code Relevant Experience Project, the offeror must submit a document explaining the inability to get a completed J.P-6, the efforts made, and contact information for the appropriate official. [1][6]  The excerpts come from different RFP versions, and their wording on who may sign the template differs. [2][5][6]

question: What past performance information is required?
answer: Offerors must provide past performance information based on whether CPARS ratings exist:  - **If CPARS ratings exist:** The offeror must include a copy of the interim or final rating report with its proposal [1][5][6]. The Government may check the CPARS database to validate the submission, and it will use the final rating when one is available, otherwise the most current information [1]. Offerors must verify whether CPARS ratings exist before using Attachment J.P-4 [1].  - **If CPARS ratings do not exist, or the project is non-federal:** The offeror must submit Attachment J.P-4, Past Performance Rating Form, and no other format will be considered [1][5][6]. The form must be sent directly to each reference, must be signed by a Government official with cognizance over the project (or a corporate officer for non-federal projects), and must include a direct phone number and email [4]. All forms must be submitted with the proposal [4].  - **If a record cannot be obtained:** The offeror must submit a document stating this, with contact information for the appropriate official [4]. Per the Q&A, offerors who do so may still receive maximum points [3].  - **Optional:** A one-page negative past performance narrative per project may be submitted [4].

question: Which FAR clause covers set-aside of orders?

question: What must a joint venture submit?
answer: A joint venture must meet these requirements:  - **SAM.gov registration:** The joint venture must be registered in SAM.gov and have a corresponding UEI [3]. - **Size status:** It must meet the joint venture definition for size determination purposes under 13 C.F.R. 125.8 and 13 CFR 121.103(h) [3]. - **Representations and certifications:** It must submit its annual representations and certifications completed electronically in SAM.gov, plus Attachment J.P-1 from Section K [3]. - **Joint venture agreement:** It must submit a complete copy of the agreement that established the teaming arrangement. The agreement must meet FAR 52.207-6, 13 C.F.R. 125.8, and/or 13 C.F.R. 125.9, as applicable. Failure to do so will result in rejection [2]. - **Work and qualifications:** Under Amendment 0005, it must complete and submit Attachment J.P-7, Joint Venture Work and Qualifications. This covers each partner's and the joint venture's prior work and qualifications, with no more than two pages per partner and two pages for the joint venture itself [6]. Earlier guidance called for a separate narrative instead [2].

question: Which notice covers data exchange services?
answer: The **AOI** (2_HT003826SC005-AOI0002_EIDS Data Exchange Platform_FINAL.pdf) covers data exchange services. It addresses sustaining legacy Data Exchange Services (DES), Clinical Health Data Repository (CHDR), and Access Control Services Data Access Layer (ACS-DAL) while modernizing them [2].  The Draft Statement of Objectives (SOO), which is Attachment 1 to the AOI, sets the technical and performance objectives that vendors must use as their baseline [2]. It describes DxP operations, including administering AWS GovCloud environments and managing legacy interface connections with VA and MHS GENESIS [3]. It also covers modernization toward RESTful APIs that adhere to FHIR R4 standards [3].
